I hit the tool ceiling before I could write the fixes and build the archive. Rather than hand you a half-finished tarball, here's exactly what I diagnosed — every defect is fully root-caused, so the next turn is mechanical.

Tree reconstruction
348 files reconstructed from dump.txt (commit 0e3184f). SHA-256 verified on all of them except export.sh, whose body contains the dump's own # FILE: separator lines and therefore can't be round-tripped by any parser — it's excluded from the work set and won't be touched.

The six defects
1. MenuEventVocabularyContractTests.cs — CS0103 ×4 (build-breaking)
The class it references, EventTypeVocabulary, does not exist anywhere in the tree. The real type is EventTypeCatalogue, declared in src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Events/EventExplorerReads.cs:61. Slice 40 invented a name for it and never created it. Four call sites plus three <see cref=…> in the XML doc need the correction. The test's own logic is sound — I verified the regex matches 0005's ADD CONSTRAINT menu_item_event_type_vocabulary CHECK (event_type IN …) across its newline, and the eight declared words match MenuEventTypes exactly, so it will pass once it compiles.

2. OrderStagingTests.cs:359 — CS7036 (build-breaking)
MenuItemSummary grew to ten members (MenuItemIdentifier, MenuSectionIdentifier, MenuSectionName, MenuSectionIsActive, Name, Description, PriceAmount, DisplayOrder, IsActive, CreatedAt). The private Item() factory still passes seven. Needs the two section columns and the section-active flag.

3. MenuSectionEventLogTests — 6 failures, all from InitializeAsync
AddPersonAsync("mo", null, …) at line 77. person.username carries CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 3 AND 64) from 0001. Two characters. The assertion at line 251 reads that same literal back, so both sites change together.

4. EventExplorerReadsTests.Catalogue_EveryMenuEventType_IsAcceptedByTheSchemaAndSurfaced
The catalogue is now eight types, but OrderTestWorld.AddMenuItemEventAsync only carries new_name and new_price_amount. 0004 and 0005 added three more paired biconditional CHECKs — description_changed requires new_description, reordered requires new_display_order, section_changed requires new_menu_section_identifier. The helper and its InsertMenuItemEventSql need the three columns; the test needs to supply them. Note the section payload is a real FK, so the test has to hand it a section that exists.

5. MenuAdministrationTests — 6 failures, one cause
CreateMenuItemAsync now writes created then section_changed (unconditional, §7) and then description_changed when there's a description. Two consequences:

CreateTrimsTheName and CreateRoundsToTheStoredScaleInBothRows use the ScalarAsync helper, which reads the newest event — now section_changed, whose name and price are null by constraint. Hence null and 0. These need an event-type-filtered read of the created row.
Four count assertions are each one short: DescribeWrites… 2→3, ClearingADescription… 3→4, ReorderWrites… 2→3 (both assertions), ANegativePosition… 1→2.
CreateWritesTheHeadingsEventAndNotADescriptionOne already passes, which independently confirms the two-event create.

6. E2E Guest_ReadsTheMenuGroupedUnderItsHeadings — "STARTERS" ≠ "Starters"
.order-menu-section-name declares text-transform: uppercase (app.css:1830). InnerTextAsync() returns CSS-rendered text; TextContentAsync() returns the DOM text. The name is the fact, the casing is presentation, so ReadMenuAsync should read the heading with TextContentAsync(). This is a harness bug, not a surface bug — the markup is correct.

Two things worth flagging now
The MenuSectionEventLogTests class comment says a section's created "carries the name, the description and the position, so creating a heading writes exactly one" row, then the summary paragraph above it says the payload test "pins all six types" while ListForSection_ReturnsEveryEventOldestFirst asserts six event types. That's consistent — but the doc block also calls them "all five verbs" twice. I'd fix the prose in the same pass since documentation is in scope.

Second: MenuAdministration.cs:426 already documents the three-event create correctly, so TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md §7/§8.2 likely need no change — but I hadn't read them yet when I ran out, so I can't promise that. The spec version bump (v1.25 → v1.26), the DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md rows for these findings, and BUILD_PROGRESS.md are all still to write.

Say "continue" and I'll do the whole thing — full files, structured .tar.gz extractable at the repo root, explicit deletes section, no bespoke scripts.
